name: Lebanon FMM HACT Quality Rules
description: Quality assessment rules for Lebanon Field Monitoring Module. Implements the 6-rule HACT Quality Check spec: Completeness, Evidence Sufficiency (Q2), HACT Activities Alignment (Q1-Q2), General Observations Coherence (narrative-Q1/Q2), Q3 Quality, and Overall Finding Quality.

rules.name: Report Completeness
rules.description: Key HACT fields must be present: narrative_finding (General Observation), overall_finding_rating, Q1, and Q2. Missing fields indicate an incomplete report.
rules.flag_template: R1: Incomplete monitoring report — missing: {missing_fields}

rules.name: Question Answer Completeness
rules.description: Measures what percentage of FMM questions were answered. Below 80% indicates incomplete data collection. Below 50% indicates severely incomplete data collection.
rules.flag_template: R2: Only {value}% of monitoring questions answered (target: 80%+)

rules.name: Narrative Evidence Quality
rules.description: Merged evidence-quality rule covering narrative sufficiency, specificity, and depth. The report should show concrete, independently observed evidence with enough detail to support findings rather than generic or boilerplate text.
rules.flag_template: R3: Q2 lacks specific or disaggregated activity evidence — {ai_detail}

rules.name: HACT Activities Alignment
rules.description: Q1 (implementation status) must be logically consistent with Q2 (activities verified). If Q1 says On-track but Q2 lists no real activities, or Q1 says Off-track but Q2 describes only positive results, the answers are misaligned.
rules.flag_template: R5: Q1 and Q2 are misaligned — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Narrative and Rating Coherence
rules.description: Merged coherence rule covering implementation status, narrative consistency, and rating alignment. Q1, Q2, the narrative, and the overall finding rating should tell a consistent story without contradictions or unsupported conclusions.
rules.hact_spec: Rule 4 - General Observations Coherence with Q1/Q2
rules.flag_template: R6: General Observation is incoherent, duplicates Q2, or does not address visit objective — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Action Point Quality
rules.description: Merged action-quality rule covering Q3 quality, SMARTness, and action-point specificity. Follow-up actions should be concrete, assigned, time-bound where possible, and directly useful for correcting the issues described in the visit.
rules.flag_template: R7: Q3 has quality issues — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Action Points Cross-Check
rules.description: Merged action cross-check rule covering issue-to-action alignment across the narrative, Q1/Q2, the summary, and available action-points records. When problems or recommendations are documented, corresponding follow-up actions must be present and clearly linked.
rules.flag_template: R8: Bottlenecks or issues identified in narrative/Q1/Q2 but Q3 lacks corresponding action points — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Challenge-to-Action Alignment
rules.description: Checks whether each key challenge or bottleneck identified in the summary (Q1, Q2, narrative_finding) has a corresponding action point in the Action Points tab. Passes when the visit is clearly positive and no follow-up is needed, or when the main challenges each have matching actions. Fails when a significant challenge is documented but not addressed by any action point, or when action points focus on minor issues while the key problems are left unaddressed.
rules.flag_template: R32: Key challenge lacks a corresponding action point — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Programme Coverage
rules.description: Merged programme-coverage rule covering multi-dimension and multi-category coverage. The report should reflect the programme dimensions relevant to the entity and visit context rather than focusing too narrowly on a single aspect of implementation.
rules.flag_template: R9: Narrative does not cover non-HACT programme dimensions — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Determinant Coverage Breadth
rules.description: Entity-adapted determinant coverage check from fmq_answered_categories. CP Output must cover Reach + Quality at minimum. Partner must cover HACT + PSEA. PD/SSFA assessed via narrative (no fm_questions categories expected). More categories covered = higher score.
rules.flag_template: R10: Insufficient determinant coverage for {entity_type} — categories covered: {value}

rules.name: Method Triangulation
rules.description: Reliability requires triangulation across data collection methods: Key Informant Interviews (KII), Focus Group Discussions (FGD), and Direct Observation. Scored from method_count (distinct collection_method values used across all answered questions in the visit). FGD cannot be used for remote monitoring visits.
rules.flag_template: R11: Only {value} data collection method(s) used — KII + FGD + Observation triangulation recommended

rules.name: PSEA/AAP Compliance
rules.description: Merged compliance rule covering PSEA, safeguarding, and AAP expectations. Relevant reports should document beneficiary protection, safeguarding measures, complaint mechanisms, and community feedback considerations where applicable.
rules.flag_template: R12: PSEA/AAP compliance gap — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Beneficiary Disaggregation
rules.description: For people-facing activities (health, education, nutrition, cash assistance, protection, psychosocial support, training, community outreach), Q2 and the narrative must include disaggregated beneficiary counts — at minimum sex breakdown (boys/girls or men/women), ideally with age groups. Activities that directly serve individuals without any numeric beneficiary data are incomplete. Non-people-facing activities (supply delivery, infrastructure checks, document review, coordination meetings) are exempt. Reports may be in English, French, or Arabic.
rules.flag_template: R13: People-facing activities listed without disaggregated beneficiary data (sex/age breakdown) — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Red Flag Intensity
rules.description: Red flags are bottom-tier Likert answers: answer <= 2 for 5-class scales; answer = 1 for 3-class scales. High red flag counts signal serious programme concerns. Scored from red_flag_count column computed during question aggregation.
rules.flag_template: R14: {value} red-flag Likert response(s) detected — serious programme concerns requiring documented corrective action

rules.name: Access Constraint Documentation
rules.description: SoP-specific: When a visit is affected by access restrictions (checkpoint delays, area closures, security incidents, evacuation), the narrative must document: (1) the nature of the restriction, (2) its impact on monitoring scope and completeness, (3) any alternative arrangements made (phone interview, secondary source, community informant). Undocumented access constraints are a significant quality gap in the SoP context.
rules.flag_template: R15: Access constraints not adequately documented — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Humanitarian Context Relevance
rules.description: SoP-specific: The narrative should be grounded in the actual humanitarian context at the time of the visit. For Gaza visits: operational status under conflict conditions, displacement, infrastructure damage. For West Bank visits: movement restrictions, Area A/B/C access considerations. Generic narratives that ignore the specific SoP operating environment score low on this dimension.
rules.flag_template: R16: Narrative lacks SoP humanitarian context relevance — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Cross-Sectoral Integration and Follow-up
rules.description: AI checks whether the report acknowledges relevant cross-sectoral linkages (e.g. Health + Nutrition, WASH + Education, CP + AAP) and whether findings or action points from previous visits to the same partner or site have been followed up on.
rules.flag_template: R17: Cross-sectoral integration or follow-up gaps — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Evidence Documentation and Depth
rules.description: Merged evidence-documentation rule covering evidence depth and attachment support. Strong reports cite sources, document verifiable observations, and include supporting attachments or equivalent documentation when required by the monitoring modality.
rules.flag_template: R18: Evidence documentation insufficient — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Evidence and Source Reliability
rules.description: Disabled — merged into R3. Both rules use the same AI prompt key (evidence_sufficiency). R3 (Narrative Evidence Quality) already covers source triangulation and reliability as part of its broader evidence quality assessment. Enabling R4 alongside R3 would run the identical AI prompt twice and apply a duplicate deduction for the same finding. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R4: Assessment lacks sufficient evidence base or multi-source triangulation — {ai_detail}

rules.name: Supporting Attachments Presence
rules.description: Checks that at least one supporting document was attached to the report. Partner and PD/SSFA visits should include verifiable evidence — photos, distribution lists, field observation notes, or signed documents. Reports with zero attachments lack documentary backing for their findings. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R28: No supporting attachments uploaded — Partner and PD/SSFA visits should include documentation (photos, distribution records, or field notes)

rules.name: Information Source Triangulation
rules.description: Checks that at least two distinct data collection methods were used (KII, FGD, Observation). Single-method reports lack the cross-source verification expected by SCO quality standards — findings should be triangulated across at least two information channels. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R31: Single data collection method used — SCO quality standards require triangulation across at least two methods (KII, FGD, and/or Observation)

rules.name: Field Office - Team Member Validation
rules.description: Validates that the monitor (team_members email) is assigned to the field office stated in the report. Reference data: populate field_office_emails map in this rules file. Rules skip silently while this map is empty.
rules.flag_template: R19: Monitor {value} is not listed as staff for field office '{key_value}' — verify assignment

rules.name: Location - PD/SSFA Site Validation
rules.description: For PD/SSFA visits, validates that the visited location (location_pcode) is one of the PD/SSFA registered sites for this partner. Skips if entity_type is not PD/SSFA or if reference_map is empty. Populate reference_map with {partner_name: [pcode1, pcode2]} to activate.
rules.flag_template: R20: Location pcode '{value}' is not a registered PD/SSFA site for partner '{key_value}'

rules.name: Section - CP Output Alignment
rules.description: For CP Output visits, validates that the section(s) monitored align with the sections associated with the selected CP output. Populate cp_output_sections with {cp_output_code: [section1, section2]} to activate.
rules.flag_template: R21: Section '{value}' does not match expected sections for CP output '{key_value}'

rules.name: Report Reviewer - PME Staff Check
rules.description: Validates that the person responsible (person_responsible_email) is a PME staff member. Note: this uses person_responsible_email as a proxy — the FMM form does not capture a distinct reviewer field. Populate reference_list to activate.
rules.flag_template: R22: Person responsible '{value}' is not in the PME staff list — confirm report has been reviewed by PME

rules.name: PD Reference Locations
rules.description: Stores registered PD/SSFA physical locations per partner for map overlay. Populate reference_map with {partner_name: [{name, lat, lon, pcode}, ...]} via the Rules UI. Used by the Visit Map to show planned vs actual visited locations. Deduction is 0 — this rule stores reference data only.
rules.flag_template: R23: Visit location '{value}' not among registered PD locations for partner '{key_value}'

rules.name: Supplies Dimension Coverage
rules.description: Checks that at least one Supplies/Products question was answered during data collection for PD-type visits. Supplies questions assess whether key inputs met agreed quality standards, were delivered on time, and are adequate in quantity. Scoped to PD only — PD/SSFA visits are covered by R29, which references the specific SCO mandatory questions (Q62–Q67) for that entity type. Applying this rule to PD/SSFA alongside R29 would cause a double deduction for the same gap. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R24: Supplies/Products dimension not covered — no supply-related questions answered during this visit

rules.name: Acceptability Dimension Coverage
rules.description: Checks that at least one Acceptability question was answered during data collection for PD-type visits. Acceptability questions assess whether intended users are satisfied with services, whether socio-cultural barriers restrict access, and whether excluded groups have been identified. Scoped to PD only — PD/SSFA visits are covered by R30, which references the specific SCO mandatory questions (Q26, Q29) for that entity type. Applying this rule to PD/SSFA alongside R30 would cause a double deduction for the same gap. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R25: Acceptability dimension not covered — no acceptability questions answered during this visit

rules.name: PSEA Mandatory Question Coverage — Partner
rules.description: For Partner visits, checks that the PSEA dimension was answered during data collection. SCO mandatory questions Q1 (proportion of beneficiaries who can explain a PSEA reporting channel) and Q2 (visible PSEA materials at the site) are both mandatory for Partner visits. No PSEA entry in fmq_answered_categories means these mandatory questions were entirely skipped. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R26: PSEA dimension not collected — SCO mandatory questions Q1 and Q2 (beneficiary PSEA knowledge and visible materials) were not answered during this Partner visit

rules.name: Community Engagement Mandatory Coverage — CP Output
rules.description: For CP Output visits, checks that Community Engagement and Accountability dimension questions were answered. SCO mandatory questions Q15 (community feedback mechanism), Q16 (community/beneficiary feedback), and Q17 (engagement with community structures) are all mandatory for CP Output visits. A missing Community Engagement category in fmq_answered_categories indicates these mandatory questions were skipped. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R27: Community Engagement dimension not collected — SCO mandatory questions Q15/Q16/Q17 (community feedback mechanism and community engagement) were not answered during this CP Output visit

rules.name: Supplies Mandatory Coverage — PD/SSFA
rules.description: PD/SSFA visits must assess the Supplies dimension (availability, timeliness, quality, fair distribution). Questions Q62–Q67 are specific to PD/SSFA entity type and cover the full supplies chain from availability through end-use. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R29: Supplies dimension not collected — PD/SSFA visits must address supplies availability, timeliness, quality, and distribution (SCO mandatory questions Q62–Q67)

rules.name: Acceptability Mandatory Coverage — PD/SSFA
rules.description: PD/SSFA visits must assess the Acceptability dimension — socio-cultural barriers, cost barriers, continuity of use, and user satisfaction. SCO mandatory questions Q26 (continuity) and Q29 (socio-cultural barriers) are required for all PD/SSFA visits except warehouse-only monitoring. [Inherited from Sudan as part of the canonical 32-rule set; disabled by default — enable and customise reference data for Lebanon before use.]
rules.flag_template: R30: Acceptability dimension not collected — PD/SSFA visits must assess socio-cultural barriers, cost barriers, and continuity of use (SCO mandatory questions Q26, Q29)
